findings.issue: The handler/isBuildRender/404-status/document-title/notFound boilerplate is copy-pasted across five dynamic routes; adding a similar section (e.g. Items) duplicates it again.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small factory, e.g. defineResourceRoute({ load, title, template }), in components/ or lib/, and let it own the build-render guard and 404 handling.

findings.issue: isBuildRender is a per-route convention: a new route that forgets the guard will fetch the live API during the build render with a stub hostname, violating the spec's no-build-time-fetch rule.
findings.suggestion: Make the guard impossible to forget — either apply it inside the shared route factory, or short-circuit api()/apiRequired() themselves when the request URL host is the build stub.

findings.issue: Card ordering is implemented independently in cardsForPokemon, getTeamCards (insertion order) and getPokemonIndex, with no comparator seam; a blanket 'sort by name' change would also break home pagination and wrongly reorder the team page.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit sort option (e.g. sortCards(cards, 'id' | 'name')) used by every list, keeping getTeamCards on insertion order by design.

findings.issue: Client islands depend on implicit DOM contracts with server templates: team-toggle assumes the first button and a .team-toggle__note span, moves-panel selects '#move-tables', and team-page refresh re-selects the 'team-page' tag defined in routes/team.ts:22.
findings.suggestion: Keep the contract explicit — a comment at each template site naming the island, or pass selectors via data attributes rather than structural assumptions.

findings.issue: lib/data.ts is a single 425-line module holding all API shapes plus per-resource lookups plus team-feature view models (getTeamCards, getTypeCoverage); every new resource section grows it further.
findings.suggestion: Split API shapes into a types module and move team builders (getTeamCards/getTypeCoverage) next to the team route or into lib/team's server half.

findings.issue: The Card.hidden / 'Hidden ability' rendering exists only for the Abilities page; removing that feature leaves this field and note as unfindable dead code.
findings.suggestion: Either co-locate the hidden-ability note with the ability route or note in the Card type that 'hidden' is abilities-only so a future removal catches it.

findings.issue: Name-validation regex is duplicated: inline in getSpecies and again as validName at data.ts:416; the 'typeLabels.get(x) ?? humanize(x)' fallback is likewise repeated in five sites (data.ts:208,384; moves/[name].ts:32; pokemon/[name].ts:68; types/[name].ts:25).
findings.suggestion: Use validName everywhere and add a typeBadgeFrom(name, labels) helper so fallback semantics have one definition.

findings.issue: export const moveTables is exported from a route module but imported nowhere; exporting template helpers from route files invites cross-route imports and blurs the route-as-entry-point convention.
findings.suggestion: Drop the export (local use only), or move the move-table renderer into components/ if it is ever shared.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: Base URL, TTL, cache dedup, concurrency limit and the media/sprite path are all defined in lib/api.ts; no other file references the API, and nothing else hardcodes localhost or fetches.

summary: This is a well-factored small app: one renderer per concept (cardLink, section, count), a single data-source module, and an isomorphic cookie seam made the team feature a clean, low-blast-radius addition. The recurring cost is copy-paste at the route layer — the handler/notFound boilerplate and the build-render guard are repeated in every route, so the next similar feature duplicates code and a new route can silently violate the no-build-time-fetch rule. Ordering logic has no shared seam, which makes any cross-list change (like sorting by name) a multi-site, partially unsafe edit.
